messages:
devops-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT 4067901234 - spike in 5xx for client 'TideMark' on dedicated pool 'dedicated-11'. Error rate peaked 22% (5m window). Auto-pager triggered.
eli (oncall): I'm on the bridge. tagging eng-runtime and SRE. Has anyone correlated with infra events?
mina (eng-runtime): looking now. I see repeated GPU process restarts on host gpu-11-4 starting 02:13:11 UTC. Container logs show repeated assertion failures in model-worker: `AssertionError: kv_cache index mismatch` and then restart. stack excerpt attached.
sara (sre): checking routing — TideMark traffic is exclusively pinned to dedicated-11 (by customer request). There is no automatic fallback configured. That explains full customer impact.
eli (oncall): immediate plan: (A) take gpu-11-4 out of rotation, (B) enable temporary cross-pool failover to our 'regional-fallback' pool for TideMark, (C) capture impacted request ids for credit calc and legal. Any objections?
mina (eng-runtime): no objections. adding note: failure appears tied to a custom model variant that TideMark uses (tide-v2-longctx). It uses extended KV cache layout. My worry: if we route to regional-fallback, we need a compatible model variant or we must downgrade to tide-v2-shortctx which may truncate long contexts — need customer approval for truncation behavior.
support_jorge: pinged TideMark ops (ops@tidemark.io). They replied: "We prefer failover over truncation. If you can keep contexts whole on fallback, please do that. Otherwise we need to schedule maintenance." Awaiting device logs from them.
eli (oncall): mine — can we spin up a temporary dedicated-compatible instance in shared pool with the same model variant? What's ETA?
mina (eng-runtime): we can provision a compat-node with same model binary but it'll take ~6 minutes to pull weights to a shared-hosted G5x2 host (we've pre-built a compat image). Suggest route to regional-fallback with a forced model-variant override to tide-v2-longctx@compat. Doing that now.
devops-bot: orchestration: creating instance group 'temp-compat-406790' -> provisioning started.
mina (eng-runtime): applied routing override: `PATCH /routing/overrides {"customer":"tidemark","to_pool":"regional-fallback","model_override":"tide-v2-longctx@compat","until":"2026-03-16T03:00:00Z"}` propagation ~8s.
eli (oncall): metrics: 5xx falling from 22% -> 6% over 4m. p95 latency decreased back toward baseline. Good. Keep monitoring.
sara (sre): forensic note: OOMs not primary; root appears to be kv cache index corruption when handling >128k context tokens due to a bug in the custom loader. We'll need to confirm whether this corrupts persisted state — initial read: no external customer data leaked, only internal model memory faults.
mina (eng-runtime): uploading diagnostic bundle `s3://redwood-incidents/4067901234/diag.tgz` (traces, coredumps, model hashes). Also captured the exact model build id tide-v2-longctx@20260313-8f3a.
support_jorge: TideMark responded: "Okay to route to fallback as long as model behavior is identical. We'd like to be on the canary window to observe. Also please include any user-visible request ids for our compliance team." I've requested their list for cross-check.
rachel (acct-mgr): note the SLA: enterprise plan with 99.99 uptime and a contractual incident credit clause. Please capture the exact impact window and # of failed requests. We'll propose credits per contract if outage > 5m.
eli (oncall): action items and owners: mina -> full root-cause draft + build diff (due 48h); sara -> runbook to prevent KV cache corruption + automated node fencing (INF-6201) ; support_jorge -> customer comm draft + impacted request ids; rachel -> exec summary + credit calc.
mina (eng-runtime): one more: I recommend we create a tenant-isolation safety net: default for all dedicated pools should include a route-to-fallback rule that is opt-out by customer. I'll draft a change request (INF-6202). This would've avoided manual failover.
sara (sre): opening incidents tickets: INF-6201 (kv-cache hardening), INF-6203 (fallback default policy), INF-6204 (post-mortem doc). Assigning to runtime & infra.
support_jorge: customer update draft: "TideMark ops — we detected elevated errors for your dedicated pool at 02:13 UTC. We initiated a controlled failover to a compat instance at 02:19 UTC, and stabilized service at 02:22 UTC. Root cause appears to be corruption in the model KV cache loader for long-context traffic; we're preparing a full RCA and timeline. If you want to participate in canary verification before we revert your traffic to dedicated-11, please let us know windows that work for you." Any edits?
rachel (acct-mgr): add estimated ETA for RCA (72 hours) and an offer to discuss credits. Also offer a dedicated exec sync within 24 hours.
eli (oncall): approved. support_jorge, send now and cc: rachel. keep routing override in place until we complete canary and confirm model integrity on dedicated-11.
mina (eng-runtime): starting canary of compatibility image on 'temp-compat-406790' (2 instances) for 20m. Will run long-context synthetic tests and a small percentage of live traffic (1%).
devops-bot: canary job started id=canary-406790, state=running.
sara (sre): while canary runs, we should mark the original host gpu-11-4 as quarantined and audit similar nodes for same model binary hash. running query for nodes with tide-v2-longctx@20260313-8f3a.
mina (eng-runtime): found two more hosts with same build; isolating them and scheduling immediate preemptive restart of model-manager on those nodes.
support_jorge: TideMark ops asked to be included in canary observations. I've scheduled a 30m shared window starting 02:45 UTC and invited their SREs.
rachel (acct-mgr): drafting exec one-pager to include timeline, customer impact (approx 4.8k requests affected, ~0.6% of hourly baseline), mitigation steps taken, and proposed credit band (per SLA, estimating 4 hours-equivalent credit if they choose). Will circulate for review.
mina (eng-runtime): canary reports: synthetic long-context tests passing; no kv index corruption observed after forced recompile. Live sample 1% had 0.1% error rate. I'll recommend gradual traffic migration back to dedicated-11 after we patch loader and redeploy model binary.
sara (sre): keep INF-6201 assigned to runtime with high priority. Also adding a preventive: default memory limit enforcement for model-workers to reduce crash blast radius.
support_jorge: sending customer note now (cc: rachel). :email:
devops-bot: status-page update: "Incident 4067901234 - TideMark dedicated pool incidents; controlled failover performed. Mitigated. Post-incident follow-up in progress." 
eli (oncall): closing live bridge. Keep the routing override until we confirm full patch and coordinated migration back. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
